items.title: Brand value can exceed half of market capitalisation
items.claim: Interbrand's 2023 Best Global Brands ranking valued Apple's brand at around $502 billion. What's the relationship between brand value and accounting?

options.text: Brand value appears directly on the balance sheet for all firms
Under IFRS / UK GAAP, internally generated brands are not recognised as balance sheet assets; purchased brands can be. Apple's $502bn estimate is an external valuation, not a reported figure
Brand value equals market cap minus debt
Brand value has no relationship with share price

items.reveal:
IAS 38 prohibits capitalising internally generated brands; accounting wants to avoid the manipulability of self-assessed intangibles. Acquired brands (e.g. Cadbury bought by Kraft for £11.5bn in 2010) appear at acquisition cost as 'goodwill' or identified intangibles.

Interbrand, Kantar BrandZ and Brand Finance use different methodologies — discounted cash flow from brand-attributable earnings — and produce different rankings. The numbers are estimates, but the underlying point is real: a meaningful share of S&P 500 market value sits in intangibles invisible on balance sheets.
items.why: Investors price intangibles even when accountants don't book them. The gap between book and market value for brand-heavy firms is largely brand and goodwill.

items.title: Share price and intrinsic value can diverge for years
items.claim: Robert Shiller's work (Nobel 2013) showed stock prices vary much more than fundamental dividends would justify. What's the implication for share price as a measure of company performance?

options.text: Share price always equals intrinsic value at all times
Share prices can diverge from intrinsic value for extended periods (excess volatility); managers focused on quarterly share prices may make worse long-term decisions
Share price has no link to fundamentals ever
Only private firms have intrinsic value

items.reveal_title: Markets price emotions as well as cash flows
items.reveal:
Shiller's 1981 American Economic Review paper showed S&P 500 prices fluctuated 5-13x more than dividend-based fair value would justify. Tech bubble peaks (2000, 2021) and crisis troughs (2009, 2020) bookend this excess volatility.

Warren Buffett quotes Benjamin Graham: 'In the short run the market is a voting machine, in the long run a weighing machine.' Managers paid largely in stock options can be incentivised to manage the voting machine rather than build long-term weight.
items.why: Headline share price moves often reflect investor sentiment as much as company performance. Compensation and strategy that anchor on share price import this volatility.

items.title: Market research said the Walkman would fail
items.claim: Sony launched the TPS-L2 Walkman in 1979. What did market research suggest beforehand?

options.text: Strong demand from young consumers — supporting the launch
Likely failure: consumers reported they wanted recording capability, not just playback, and disliked the absence of speakers
No research was conducted because Akio Morita had no money for it

items.reveal:
Co-founder Masaru Ibuka wanted a portable player so he could listen to opera on long flights. Akio Morita, despite hostile focus group findings, championed the launch. Sony hedged by initially offering it with two headphone jacks (so you could share) and a 'hotline' button to talk to a companion — both later dropped.

First-month sales in Japan were 30,000 units. By the early 1980s the Walkman was a global phenomenon and 'walkman' became a generic word for portable cassette player.

Clayton Christensen later used the case in 'The Innovator's Dilemma' to argue that existing customer research can't reliably predict demand for genuinely new products.
items.why: Market research has methodological limits. Consumers can tell you what they want among options they already know; they're worse at imagining a category that doesn't exist.
